items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: On guitar and vocals I had a singer who was very good, played very good guitar and also sang -- his name was Norville Reed.

ctx.x: In 1950, I got this group together to work in a room that was in a hotel in Washington. It was a Black hotel, and they had a room there called the 2011 Room. They brought in big people. Like, the Nat King Cole Trio played there, George Shearing's Quintet, and we were the house band. This band that I had was six pieces, or six musicians.

The drummer I grew up with, and I might have mentioned him before -- everybody calls him Dude Brown; his name is George Brown. George Brown played drums. Frank Wess played tenor, clarinet and flute. I had a violinist whose name was Addaway Robinson, a very promising violinist and musician, but I guess for economical reasons he never chose to stick around and fight it out like a lot of the rest of us did.
